pages.heading: Profile
paragraphs: MEng Aerospace Engineering graduate (UWE Bristol, 2025, Merit) specialising in computational fluid dynamics, numerical modelling and engineering analysis. University project experience combines transient simulation, MATLAB analysis and mechanical design with critical assessment of model fidelity and test outcomes.

pages.heading: Technical Skills
bullets: CFD and aerodynamics: ANSYS Fluent; transient sliding meshes, Transition SST/SBES, FW-H acoustic analysis and comparison against reference data.

Numerical analysis: MATLAB for engineering calculations, signal processing and CFD post-processing; NASA CEA thermochemical analysis, with configuration-control limitations documented in the rocket case study.
Mechanical design: SolidWorks CAD, engineering drawings, injector sizing, manufacturing constraints and system integration; university FEA experience using ANSYS Mechanical.

Programming and tools: MATLAB, developing Python skills, foundational C++; Git/GitHub, Linux and Excel. Experience is based on university and personal projects rather than professional software-development employment.

entries.title: VAWT Aeroacoustics
entries.subtitle: Individual MEng research project | April–June 2025
bullets: Developed a transient model of a three-bladed Darrieus turbine in ANSYS Fluent, following a published Transition SST/SBES approach. Built the domain, sliding mesh and local refinement strategy.
Extended the model using FW-H acoustics at four receiver positions and MATLAB post-processing of pressure histories and frequency-domain behaviour.

At TSR 3.3 and 9 m/s, predicted power coefficient was approximately 0.13 versus approximately 0.27 in the reference study. Mesh, time-step and computational constraints limited fidelity; reliable acoustic prediction was not established.

entries.title: 600 N N₂O/HDPE Hybrid Rocket Engine
entries.subtitle: Five-person MEng capstone | November 2024–June 2025
bullets: Principal responsibility for oxidiser injector design from concept selection and analytical sizing through CFD, SolidWorks CAD, manufacture and integration, ending in a two-ring impinging configuration.
Contributed to shared propulsion sizing using NASA CEA and MATLAB, and initial nozzle calculations before detailed nozzle work passed to another team member.

Design targets were 600 N thrust, five-second nominal burn, O/F 7 and approximately 33 bar chamber pressure. Ignition occurred, but injector–chamber leakage prevented target pressure and sustained combustion. These figures are not measured performance.
